packages.label: הַצַּדִּיק וְהַחוֹתָם
packages.reason: Torah #140 teaches a single, tightly focused idea: the Tzaddik is beyond ordinary intellectual grasp ('לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׂכְלוֹ'), and yet his nature can be inferred — the way a seal's engraved letters can only be read by pressing it into wax. The Tzaddik is explicitly called a בְּחִינַת חוֹתָם (seal), because just as the seal's inscription is hidden in its reversed form, the Tzaddik's inner reality is concealed yet can be known through his disciples (the 'wax impression'). The dominant node is צדיק, which is connected to חותם (the seal). The same צדיק is also called 'כָּל הָאָדָם' (all of humanity) via the Kohelet verse — this is an additional bechina in the source text not yet in the dataset (see torah_140_additions.json). The package is good/holy: the Tzaddik and his seal are expressions of the covenant of holiness ('בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ').

stats.evil_mirror_notes: Torah #140 is entirely focused on the positive domain of the Tzaddik and his seal-nature. There is no explicit evil counterpart developed. The teaching does not discuss opposing forces, falsehood, or a 'dark side' of the seal metaphor. This is consistent with it being a micro-teaching (one teaching, one concept pair) functioning as a self-contained reflection on knowability and the Tzaddik.
